plotSections.title: The helm's soul-magic test
bullets: Carlkin treats the ornamental, hobgoblin-inspired helm Walker has been wearing as a likely lich phylactery. Walker says it is mundane and not a phylactery, and hands it over.
Carlkin dunks it in a bag of holding he enchanted to detect phylactery soul-magic and burst into flame on contact. He first thinks the test failed and offers the helm back in ten to fifteen minutes.

Walker's perception (27) catches the pouch smoldering. The bag burns slowly, like moss, rather than flashing into full flame. Carlkin says a true phylactery would have caused a full fire; this is trace soul magic plus possible other enchantments, and he accuses Walker of downplaying it.

Walker is fire-resistant and uses his golden glove to pull the helm out. The damage is negligible. The bag's interior is only a little larger than the helm; it burns through, fractures like over-tapped crystal, and drifts away burning. Walker is left with a slightly smoking white helm, cold to the touch, which Carlkin says Walker took from the Emperor.
Carlkin invites the group into the lighthouse to identify exactly what Walker has been wearing.

plotSections.title: Carlkin's study
bullets: Walker, Dana, Ciri, and Ord go in with Carlkin. Elrus, Araden, and Benji stay outside and fall into conversation.

The study floor is still a mess after only a day: the center looks like a sandbox where flagstones were heaved up. Carlkin has Walker set the helm on a small altar-like lectern and starts through papers. The reading is not finished before the scene cuts.
Dana asks what Carlkin had been saying about the little eagle; that is interrupted by the perception check and never answered.

plotSections.title: Gerk looks for Haldor
bullets: Gerk is alone in New Navel's market, seeking the sheriff. A living woman vendor, not a ghost, says Haldor may be at the tavern or at his house, and points him south-west: past the tavern, down the road, then right, to Haldor's house.

Gerk gives her a gold and buys her small basket-woven wicker chicken. She also offers a life-sized wicker goose and says she can make geese or a gander. Gerk refuses and says he has to kill geese on sight as a religious practice. The vendor two doors down, who sells only geese, stops. Gerk points at him and says he will be back.
Gerk finds Haldor at home, relaxed in a rocking chair on the porch with his boots on a stump and his hands folded, watching from under his hat brim. Gerk waves vigorously as he approaches.

chronologicalEvents: Carlkin calls the helm on Walker's head a likely lich phylactery. Walker disagrees and says it is mundane.
Carlkin notes that the helm is ornamental and hobgoblin-inspired, and Walker lets him take it.

Carlkin drops the helm into a belt pouch that opens to about two feet and snaps shut. He says a phylactery would have given itself away, then doubts that it is one and estimates ten to fifteen minutes for its return.
Carlkin explains the pouch is a bag of holding enchanted to sense phylactery soul-magic and ignite on contact, and he initially concludes the helm is not a phylactery.
Dana starts to ask about the little eagle. Walker rolls perception 27, and the pouch's bottom-right corner smolders.
Carlkin pulls the bag off his belt and throws it down. It smolders across its surface instead of bursting into flame.
Carlkin says this is not a full phylactery reaction: the helm carries trace soul magic and maybe further enchantments, and he tells Walker it does not look like an ordinary helm.

Using fire resistance and the golden glove, Walker retrieves the white helm. The bag burns out, cracks apart, and blows away. The helm is cold to the touch. Carlkin says it is the helm Walker took from the Emperor.
The lighthouse group follows Carlkin inside, leaving Elrus, Araden, and Benji outside in conversation.
In the damaged study, Walker places the helm on a small altar-lectern while Carlkin sorts papers.
Gerk asks a living market vendor for the sheriff and is directed to Haldor's house south-west of the market, by the tavern.
Gerk buys a wicker chicken for one gold, rejects a life-sized wicker goose, and says killing geese on sight is religious. He warns the goose vendor two doors down that he will be back.
Gerk reaches Haldor's porch and waves. Haldor is relaxed in a rocking chair, boots on a stump, and acknowledges him.

Helm.existing: A helm Carlkin agreed to examine, later pulled from his burning bag with Walker's golden glove.
notes: Walker has been wearing it. It is white, ornamental, and hobgoblin-inspired, and Carlkin says Walker took it from the Emperor.
Carlkin's soul-magic bag does not fully ignite. He reads that as trace soul magic and possible further enchantments, not a full phylactery.
After the bag burns away the helm is slightly smoking, then cold to the touch. Walker sets it on a small altar-like lectern in Carlkin's study for more research.
quotesThemes: Carlkin: a real phylactery would have made a full fire; this result means trace soul magic.
openQuestions: What the helm actually is, beyond trace soul magic and possible other enchantments, is still awaiting Carlkin's examination.

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like person whose lighthouse and bookshop are in New Navel.
notes: He is at his New Navel lighthouse and examines Walker's helm in person.
He enchanted a bag of holding into a soul-magic test: phylactery-level soul magic should make it burst into flame. Trace soul magic only makes it smolder, and the bag is destroyed.
He first clears the helm, then accuses Walker of lying once the bag smolders, and takes the helm into his study for a closer reading.
The test pouch expands to about two feet. He moves with a speed he jokes one would not expect of a turtle.
personality: Tests the dangerous object himself, then invites the party in to finish the identification.
quotesThemes: If it were a phylactery, contact would have been a full fire.
He can return the helm in about ten to fifteen minutes, then later says he needs the bag to finish burning before he can investigate further.
openQuestions: What he was about to say regarding the little eagle is never answered.

Carlkin's lighthouse.existing: Carlkin's home and bookshop in New Navel, previously the site of an abyss door.
notes: The study floor is still wrecked only a day later. The center looks like a sandbox where flagstones were pushed up.
A corner holds a small desk and study setup, including a small altar or lectern where the helm is placed.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter, Gatekeeper of The Reach, bonded to Glimmen.
notes: He has been wearing the white helm and does not believe it is a phylactery because he finds it mundane.
He rolls a 27 perception and notices Carlkin's pouch start to smoke.
He is fire-resistant. With the golden glove he pulls the helm from the burning bag for negligible damage, then stays with Carlkin for the follow-up study.
quotesThemes: He tells the group it is not a phylactery and that no one has to worry anymore, before the smolder changes Carlkin's reading.

Golden glove.existing: Walker's golden glove, used to pull the helm from Carlkin's burning bag.
notes: Walker uses it, with his fire resistance, to reach into the smoldering bag and retrieve the helm. Carlkin treats the resulting damage as negligible.

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric and Gatekeeper of the Pitel keystone.
notes: She is the one pressing whether Walker's helm is a phylactery, and she repeats that Carlkin said soul magic would make the bag burst into flame.
She asks what Carlkin had been saying about the little eagle. The question is dropped when Walker is told to roll perception.
She follows Carlkin into the lighthouse because she wants to see the examination.
openQuestions: She asks Carlkin what he was saying about the little eagle and does not get an answer.

Ciri.existing: Half-elf rogue, Gatekeeper connected to Lith's keystone.
notes: She whispers to Walker that the helm looks like a phylactery.
She goes into the lighthouse with the others, meaning to needle Walker.
quotesThemes: She whispers to Walker that it looks like a phylactery.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian, Doorman, and keeper of the Midgard keystone.
notes: He is away from the lighthouse group, alone in New Navel, looking for Sheriff Haldor. He asks a living vendor rather than causing a scene, then goes to the house she points out.
He pays one gold for a small wicker chicken and refuses a life-sized wicker goose.
He says killing geese on sight is a religious obligation, and he tells the goose vendor two doors down that he will be back.
He approaches Haldor's porch with a vigorous wave. Haldor has not spoken with him yet.
personality: Treats killing geese on sight as a religious duty.
quotesThemes: He tells the wicker vendor he has to kill geese on sight, and that it is a religious thing.
He points at the goose vendor and says he will be back for him.

Joanna.existing: New Navel market vendor who sells wicker animals.
notes: The wicker seller Gerk meets is a living woman, not a ghost. She holds a small basket-woven chicken and, for the same gold, also offers a one-to-one wicker goose, saying she can make geese or a gander.
She directs Gerk to Haldor: the house is south-west of the market, by the tavern, down the road and to the right.
Gerk pays her one gold and takes the wicker chicken.

Wicker chicken.existing: A small basket-woven wicker chicken Gerk buys from Joanna for one gold.
notes: Gerk buys it from the New Navel wicker vendor for one gold while asking the way to Haldor's house, and he carries it to the sheriff's house.

Goose vendor.existing: Seller two doors down from Joanna, associated with geese.
notes: Described as the vendor two doors down who has nothing but geese. He stops when Gerk says he kills geese on sight. Gerk points at him and says he will be back.

Haldor.existing: Sheriff of New Navel who bans doors and spirit-taking inside the city.
notes: A market vendor says he would be at the tavern or at his house. Gerk finds him at the house.
He is on his porch in a rocking chair, boots up on a stump, hands folded, hat brim low, relaxed. He sees Gerk coming and acknowledges him, but the conversation has not started.
personality: Appears unhurried and at ease on his own porch.

notes: Haldor's house is south-west of New Navel's market, reached by going past or behind the tavern, down the road, and turning right.
Haldor is home, seated on the porch.

New Navel.existing: A familiar trade stop and the site of Carlkin's lighthouse.
notes: The market is a small open bazaar of ordinary living vendors; Gerk specifically checks that the wicker seller is not a ghost.
The tavern is a visible landmark on the way to Haldor's house.
Carlkin calls the white helm the one Walker took from the Emperor. No other detail about the Emperor is given in this stretch.

Carlkin enchanted a bag of holding to detect soul magic of the kind associated with a phylactery and to burst into flames on contact. He describes it as a soul-cleaning apparatus he put together for this situation.
A full phylactery would cause a full fire. The helm only makes the bag smolder, which he reads as trace soul magic.

The opening expands to about two feet, but the space inside is only large enough for the helm and a little more. After Walker retrieves the helm, the bottom burns through and the rest fractures and burns away on the wind.

newTerms.name: Emperor
notes: Unidentified figure Carlkin credits as the source of the white helm Walker took and has been wearing.

newTerms.name: Soul-cleaning bag
notes: Carlkin's bag of holding, enchanted to burn on contact with phylactery soul-magic. Full phylactery magic would cause a full fire; weaker soul magic only smolders it. This bag is destroyed in the helm test.

newTerms.name: Haldor's house
notes: The sheriff's house in New Navel, south-west of the market past the tavern. Haldor is on the porch when Gerk arrives.
